items.concern: The κ=0 (mean) mode of velocity and scalar: conserved, damped, or pinned
items.reference_practice: TurTLE pins it by redundant mechanisms. Every RHS projection ends by zero-filling the κ=0 mode on the owning rank: cpp/kspace.cpp:693-698 "if (this->layout->myrank == this->layout->rank[0][0]) { std::fill_n((rnumber*)(xa), 2, 0.0); ... }" — ℙ is defined as zero at κ=0, not identity. The velocity recovered from vorticity is mean-zeroed every stage: cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:237-238 "if (this->kk->layout->myrank == 0) std::fill_n((rnumber*)this->u->get_cdata(), 6, 0.0);". symmetrize() forces the 0 mode real (cpp/field.cpp:1197-1200 "// make 0 mode real ... cdata[cc][1] = 0.0;"), an impose_zero_mode() utility exists (cpp/field.hpp:274-281), forcing bands test "(k2 > 0) && (this->fk0 <= knorm)" (cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:360-363), and the random IC fills only "if (k2 > 0)" (cpp/field.cpp:2445).
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:416-418 `_zero_mean_mode!(f) = (_zero_mean_mode_data!(field_data(f)); f)` with `fill!(view(data, 1:1, 1:1, 1:1), zero(T))`, applied in `velocity_rhs!` (src/Generator.jl:479) and `scalar_rhs!` (src/Generator.jl:632); the comment at 405-415 records the mechanism ("Every reference DNS pins this mode") and deliberately places the zeroing BETWEEN the nonlinear assembly and the forcing source so a mean-driving forcing stays expressible. The IC mean is zeroed at the source: src/State.jl:121-124 "The envelope vanishes at κ = 0, which IS the mean removal" (scalar twin at 210-212). One scoped difference from TurTLE: we pin the advective RHS and conserve the state's zero mean exactly (exp(0)=1 integrating factor), where TurTLE also re-zeroes the state each stage — a mean injected out-of-band into our state persists undamped by design.
items.consequence_if_missing: The discrete ⟨u×ω⟩ residual (nonzero only to roundoff plus aliasing) is integrated with no restoring term and grows at the Lyapunov rate — the src comment records 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps: a spurious uniform sweep that pollutes Lagrangian statistics and the CFL speed. This was the trigger finding; the fix is in the tree.

items.concern: Division by k²=0 inside the Leray/pressure projection
items.reference_practice: The projection loop simply skips the singular mode: cpp/kspace.cpp:645 and 714 "if (k2 > 0)" wrap the entire tval = (k·û)/k2 computation, so no division at κ=0 ever happens; the mode is then zero-filled (kspace.cpp:693-698). The Biot–Savart recovery guards it separately: cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:223 "const double kk2 = (k2 > 0) ? k2 : 1.;".
items.our_evidence: Our projection is the backend's `helmholtz_projection!`, called at src/Generator.jl:523-524; the backend forms the denominator as `ifelse(iszero(squared), one(squared), squared)` (PF clone, inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/DifferentialOperators.jl:268), so κ=0 is division-safe. Note the guarded projection acts as the IDENTITY at κ=0 (longitudinal part evaluates to 0, source passes through) — which is exactly why the separate `_zero_mean_mode!` pin of the item above is load-bearing on our side where TurTLE's zero-fill makes ℙ(κ=0)=0.
items.consequence_if_missing: A 0/0 at the single κ=0 mode NaNs the projected term, and one transform later the NaN is dense in every field — instant, total corruption on the first step.

items.concern: Hermitian (conjugate) symmetry of the spectral state — enforcement vs construction
items.reference_practice: TurTLE actively re-imposes it: field::symmetrize() (cpp/field.cpp:1189-1233) makes the 0 mode real, zeroes all three Nyquist planes ("// put kx = nx/2 modes to 0"), and reconciles the conjugate pairs of the kx=0 plane line by line with MPI exchanges; it is called after every nonlinear assembly, projection, forcing and step (cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:207, 239, 556, 588, 669) and on the generated IC (field.cpp:2487 "output_field->symmetrize()").
items.our_evidence: Symmetry holds by construction, with no re-enforcement pass (searched src/ for symmetrize/hermitian/conj — none exists). Every stochastic input enters spectral space through an r2c transform of a real physical field, which is Hermitian exactly: the velocity/scalar seeds at src/State.jl:113 and 204 "copyto!(field_data(noise), randn(rng, T, physical_field_shape(...)))" then `to_spectral!`; the OU forcing noise at src/Forcing.jl:747 "randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical))" then `to_spectral!` (751). Every subsequent operation — real even per-mode multipliers (dealias, integrating factor, projection with real wavenumbers), real linear combinations, and nonlinear terms that round-trip through r2c (src/Generator.jl:521 `to_spectral!(product_spectral, ω, domain.velocity_plans)`) — preserves the symmetry to the bit.
items.consequence_if_missing: Not missing, but unguarded at the boundary: a user hand-writing spectral coefficients (the `fields_modified!` escape hatch) can introduce a non-Hermitian component that nothing ever removes; spectral diagnostics and the c2r physical images would then silently disagree. TurTLE's symmetrize() would scrub it; ours documents the state as the single source of truth instead.

items.concern: Nyquist / oddball wavenumber treatment (the unpaired mode of even-N real FFTs)
items.reference_practice: TurTLE zeroes the Nyquist planes outright, every symmetrize() call (cpp/field.cpp:1202-1233), and additionally keeps every dealias cutoff below them — the SMOOTH-mode comment cpp/kspace.cpp:93-105 is explicit: "Here 'kM' = 'highest wavemode that has nonzero amplitude' ... generically kM = N/2 - 1". Its per-axis wavenumber arrays carry an unpaired +N/2 entry, harmless because the modes are always zero.
items.our_evidence: Two complementary mechanisms. (a) For TwoThirds/PhaseShift the cutoff is strictly below Nyquist — src/SimulationDomain.jl:144-147 `_retained_nyquist_fraction(::TwoThirds) = 2 // 3` etc., built into the mask at 265-269 — so the planes are removed from every assembled RHS and from the IC (src/State.jl:140 folds `domain.dealias` into the seed). (b) HouLi retains the planes damped to machine epsilon (src/SimulationDomain.jl:273-277 `strength = T(isnothing(strategy.strength) ? -log(eps(T)) : ...)`), and the backend's stated convention covers the derivative side: PF clone DifferentialOperators.jl:26-27 "first-derivative wavenumbers are zeroed at the Nyquist frequency on even-length axes, while squared wavenumbers keep the true squared wavenumber" — no sign-ambiguous derivative content can be produced, while viscous decay at Nyquist stays physical.
items.consequence_if_missing: An unpaired Nyquist mode differentiated with a signed wavenumber produces a spurious imaginary (non-real-field) contribution, and Nyquist content in products aliases with the wrong sign — a slow, silent asymmetry of the physical field.

items.concern: Sharp-mask boundary shell: is the |κ| = N/3 shell inside the 2/3 mask when 3 divides N?
items.reference_practice: TurTLE excludes the boundary twice over: the TWO_THIRDS cutoff is set one mode short — cpp/kspace.cpp:88-90 "this->kMx = this->dkx*(int(2*(int(this->layout->sizes[2])-1)/3)-1);" (i.e. (N/3 − 1)·dk) — and low_pass removes the boundary itself: cpp/kspace.cpp:286 "if (k2 >= km2) std::fill_n(...)" zeroes k = kM too.
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationDomain.jl:265-266 keeps the CLOSED ball: `_cutoff_wavenumber` = T(2/3)·T(N/2)·T(2π/L) fed to PF's `spectral_cutoff`, whose band test is inclusive (`low_squared <= squared <= high_squared`, PF clone Convolution.jl `spectral_band`). When 3 | N the shell at exactly N/3 can receive alias images of boundary-mode products (2·(N/3) − N = −N/3 lands back on the retained boundary), so exact dealiasing holds only strictly below it. Whether that shell is actually inside our mask turns on element-type rounding of the fraction: the code's own comment (src/SimulationDomain.jl:258-263) records that Float32's 2/3 "lands slightly above the exact 2/3" (boundary included) while Float64's lands below (boundary excluded by accident of rounding).
items.consequence_if_missing: A thin, weak alias contamination confined to the single outermost retained shell on 3|N grids in Float32 — visible as a spectrum blip at the cutoff, not a stability threat.

items.concern: Energy-spectrum shell-binning conventions at the first and last shell
items.reference_practice: TurTLE floor-bins — cpp/kspace.cpp:856-864 "if (k2 <= this->kM2) { const int tmp_int = int(std::sqrt(k2) / this->dk)..." — restricted to the dealiased band, weights the rfft half-spectrum by nxmodes (1 on the kx=0 plane, 2 otherwise; the six-argument CLOOP in kspace.hpp), and records per-shell mode counts and mean |k| with a guarded division (kspace.cpp:148-152 "if (k2 < this->kM2) ... nshell_local_thread..."; 199-201 "if (this->nshell[n] > 0) this->kshell[n] /= this->nshell[n];").
items.our_evidence: Ours round-bins to CENTERED shells over all modes out to the corner: PF clone Reductions.jl:1076 "shell = round(Int, sqrt(squared) / fundamental)" with the rfft weight 1 on the folded axis's zero and even-Nyquist planes, 2 otherwise (Reductions.jl:1077-1079 and `_parseval_weight` 926-934 — TurTLE's nxmodes convention exactly), documented to refine the inner product exactly (∑ shells = ⟨f,f⟩) with ties-to-even at half-integer boundaries. Consumed at src/Observables.jl:327-329: `energy_spectrum` returns the per-shell energy E_n = P/2, documented as per-shell energy vs density (docstring at 305-325).
items.consequence_if_missing: Half-bin abscissa shifts and first/last-shell distortion when comparing against a floor-binned reference spectrum; both sides are internally consistent, so the risk is only cross-code comparison done without noting the convention.

items.concern: CFL handling: who chooses Δt and what guards the choice
items.reference_practice: TurTLE takes dt as a fixed input parameter (cpp/full_code/NSVE.cpp:231 reads "parameters/dt") and only MONITORS the CFL velocity as a per-snapshot diagnostic: compute_CFL_velocity() takes the grid max of |u1|+|u2|+|u3| (cpp/field.cpp:199-236) and NSVE::do_stats writes it as a time series (NSVE.cpp:209-216). No adaptivity, no in-run stability enforcement.
items.our_evidence: Ours is adaptive and guarded: Δt = C·Δx/max|u| with the ceiling C declared per scheme and NO silent fallback (src/Propagator.jl:600-605 "_base_cfl(::IFRK2) = 0.25; _base_cfl(::IFLowStorageRK3) = 0.5" — the comment records the deleted 0.3 fallback), corrected for the retained dealias band (Propagator.jl:610-611 `* (2 // 3) / _retained_nyquist_fraction(domain.dealiasing)`), floored against the decaying-flow step runaway by a resolution bound 1/(D·κ_min²) and a caller max_dt (src/SimulationRun.jl:514-520), and the Δt > 0 invariant checked on both routes (SimulationRun.jl:547-549). One convention difference: TurTLE's monitored speed is the per-point L1 component sum (stricter by up to √3 than our per-point Euclidean max, src/Observables.jl:177 `max_speed(u) = maximum(norm, u)`); our C is the calibrated ceiling for that convention, so the pair is internally consistent.
items.consequence_if_missing: With a fixed dt and no monitor, a transient that raises u_max past the stability boundary blows the run up silently; with adaptivity but no runaway floor, a decaying flow drives Δt → ~1e15 and the integrating factor annihilates the state (the measured failure recorded in the src comment).

items.concern: Forcing normalization when the forced band is (near-)empty
items.reference_practice: An explicit epsilon floor before the divide: cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:385-386 "if (energy_in_shell < 10*std::numeric_limits<rnumber>::epsilon()) energy_in_shell = 1;" — the fixed-injection amplitude injection_rate/energy_in_shell can then never diverge (the same pattern guards the fixed_energy rescale).
items.our_evidence: A scale-free positivity guard instead of an absolute floor: src/Forcing.jl:89 "_band_is_empty(band_value) = !(isfinite(band_value) && band_value > zero(band_value))", applied by ConstantPower (Forcing.jl:645 "return _band_is_empty(band_observable) ? 0.0 : injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)"), VarianceController (618), and VarianceRescaling (385 "nothing in the band yet"). The comment at 78-88 argues the design: the scalar equation is exactly linear in φ, so any constant floor breaks the φ → sφ symmetry and silently switches the forcing off for small-amplitude (especially Float32) runs — the empty band is left alone rather than floored to an arbitrary scale, and the docstring warns to seed content in the band (Forcing.jl:478-482).
items.consequence_if_missing: Division by a ~0 band energy hands the forcing an unbounded amplitude — one step from an empty band to a blown-up run; TurTLE floors it, we zero it, both prevent the kick.

items.concern: Forcing must never reach the κ=0 mode
items.reference_practice: Every band membership test excludes it explicitly: cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:360-363 "if ((k2 > 0) && (this->fk0 <= knorm) && (this->fk1 >= knorm))" for the injection-rate normalization, and 440 "if (k2 > 0)" inside impose_forcing's energy sums.
items.our_evidence: Bands are annuli from (lowest_shell − ½)·2π/L with lowest_shell defaulting to 1 (src/Forcing.jl:266-268 `_shell_band` → `spectral_band(..., (lowest - 0.5) * k0, (highest + 0.5) * k0)`), so κ=0 sits outside every default band; a lowest_shell = 0 attempt cannot slip through because the backend band constructor rejects a negative lower edge (PF clone Convolution.jl, `spectral_band`: "band edges must satisfy 0 <= low <= high"). The OU noise's own κ=0 component (physical randn has a nonzero mean) is removed by the same band convolve (src/Forcing.jl:749 `convolve!(noise_spectral, noise_spectral, ou.band)`).
items.consequence_if_missing: A forcing that touches κ=0 pumps a uniform momentum the integrating factor conserves forever (exp(0)=1) — the same undamped-mean pathology as the trigger bug, but actively driven.

items.concern: Blow-up / non-finite state detection during the run
items.reference_practice: TurTLE has no field-level NaN check in the time loop; the only asserts are debug-build particle checks — cpp/particles/particles_system.hpp:546-555 "void checkNan() const { // TODO remove ... assert(std::isnan(my_particles_positions[...]) == false);" — and divergence surfaces post-hoc through the recorded statistics (histogram bounds set by max_velocity_estimate, NSVE.cpp:207).
items.our_evidence: Every advance! hard-fails on the state it just produced, after the closing deposit: src/SimulationRun.jl:579-588 "isfinite(max_speed(sim.cache)) || error(\"non-finite velocity at step ... the run appears to have blown up\")" plus the separate scalar check ("a passive scalar cannot feed back into the velocity, so a scalar that has gone non-finite leaves the guarded quantity perfectly finite" — checked at 586-588); the adaptive path re-checks at src/SimulationRun.jl:483.
items.consequence_if_missing: A run that blows up keeps stepping on NaNs — wasted GPU hours and a poisoned statistics stream, discovered only at analysis time. We exceed the reference here.

items.concern: Checkpoint / exact-restart and mid-run reproducibility
items.reference_practice: TurTLE checkpoints the full spectral state per checkpoint file and stores the INTEGER iteration and checkpoint counters in HDF5, re-read on startup (cpp/full_code/direct_numerical_simulation.cpp:53-121 read_iteration/write_iteration; NSVE.cpp:140-144 write_checkpoint → io_checkpoint); all forcing time-dependence is derived from the integer counter — cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:605 "this->omega_nonlin(0, this->iteration*dt);" — so a restarted run replays the identical trajectory with no accumulated-float ambiguity.
items.our_evidence: Searched src/ for restart, checkpoint, save, write, serialize, JLD, HDF5: no state-serialization surface exists — the only `restart!` is the particle scheme's history clear (src/SimulationRun.jl:602, src/Particles.jl:247). The clock accumulates Float64 time (src/SimulationRun.jl:589 `sim.clock.time += Δt` — inherent to the adaptive step, unlike TurTLE's fixed-dt integer clock), and StochasticOU carries a private MersenneTwister plus an OU state field (src/Forcing.jl:726) with no capture/restore offered. Reproducibility from t=0 IS provided (the `seed` keyword, Forcing.jl:698 "The `seed` (default 0) fixes the random stream, so a forced run is reproducible"; the Simulation `rng` keyword, SimulationRun.jl:176-177) — but a long run cannot be resumed exactly, or at all, without the caller inventing their own serialization of state + clock + forcing internals + tracer positions.
items.consequence_if_missing: A multi-day run lost to a crash restarts from t=0; a stochastic-forced or particle-carrying run cannot be split across sessions with a defensible claim of statistical continuity. No wrong physics — an operational gap.

items.concern: Initial-condition sanitization before the first step (solenoidal, band-limited, symmetric, mean-free)
items.reference_practice: The generated IC is passed through the full scrub before step 1: cpp/full_code/NSVE.cpp:103-119 — make_gaussian_random_field (amplitudes only at "if (k2 > 0)", field.cpp:2445), then "this->fs->kk->template project_divfree<rnumber>(...); compute_curl(...); this->fs->kk->template low_pass<rnumber, THREE>(..., this->fs->kk->kM); this->fs->cvorticity->symmetrize();".
items.our_evidence: The seed pipeline applies the same invariants in one pass each: src/State.jl:113 (real physical noise → r2c, Hermitian by construction), 138-141 — the envelope (zero at κ=0, the mean removal, 121-124) is composed with the dealias kernel in a single convolve "convolve!(û, û, convolve(envelope, domain.dealias))" then "helmholtz_projection!(û, û, domain.multipliers)" — followed by the energy rescale that THROWS if the band was annihilated (State.jl:147-151 "the seeded velocity has no energy to rescale...") instead of silently returning a zero field.
items.consequence_if_missing: A non-solenoidal or above-band IC injects divergence and alias content the first RHS then propagates; a mean-carrying seed sweeps every tracer (the src comment records 13.5% of the seeded energy landing in the mean without the κ=0 guard).

items.concern: Keeping the evolving state itself inside the dealiased band (state truncation each stage vs by induction)
items.reference_practice: TurTLE re-truncates the state at every stage: each step's CLOOP writes only "if (k2 <= this->kk->kM2)" with the destination pre-zeroed (cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:594-607, and the *this->v[1] = 0.0 at 599), and compute_vorticity/compute_velocity zero everything beyond the band (cpp/vorticity_equation.cpp:203-204, 233-234 "else std::fill_n(..., 6, 0.0);").
items.our_evidence: The truncation is applied to the assembled nonlinear term inside the projection's own pass (src/Generator.jl:523-524, the kernel-composed `helmholtz_projection!(out, product_spectral, domain.multipliers, kernel)`) and to the IC (src/State.jl:140); the state then stays in-band by induction — the integrating factor is diagonal decay and every RHS is truncated — with no per-step state sweep (deliberately one pass fewer; the comments at Generator.jl:466-475 record the fold). HouLi legitimately carries damped near-Nyquist state content, so a hard state sweep would be wrong for it anyway.
items.consequence_if_missing: The induction has one unguarded edge: content hand-written above the band (through the `fields_modified!` escape hatch) is only viscously damped, never removed, and PhaseShift's exactness argument presumes no state content above its cutoff. In the normal loop the invariant provably holds.

lanes.mean_mode: TurTLE never lets the κ=0 velocity mode evolve, through layered, redundant mechanisms rather than one. (1) The Leray projection is DEFINED as zero at κ=0, not identity: project_divfree skips the singular mode in the loop (cpp/kspace.cpp:645 and 714 "if (k2 > 0)") and then explicitly zero-fills it on the rank that owns it — cpp/kspace.cpp:693-698 "if (this->layout->myrank == this->layout->rank[0][0]) { std::fill_n((rnumber*)(xa), 2, 0.0); std::fill_n((rnumber*)(ya), 2, 0.0); std::fill_n((rnumber*)(za), 2, 0.0); }". Since force_divfree wraps this (kspace.hpp:300-302) and is called after every nonlinear assembly and every RK substage (vorticity_equation.cpp:555, 587, 622, 644, 668; NSE.cpp:369, 487, 509), the RHS mean is scrubbed every evaluation and the advanced state's mean every substep. (2) In the primary (vorticity-form) solver the mean velocity is not even part of the state: the velocity is recovered from vorticity each stage with the Biot–Savart division guarded ("const double kk2 = (k2 > 0) ? k2 : 1.;", vorticity_equation.cpp:223) and the κ=0 mode zero-filled outright (vorticity_equation.cpp:237-238 "if (this->kk->layout->myrank == 0) std::fill_n((rnumber*)this->u->get_cdata(), 6, 0.0);"). (3) field::symmetrize(), called after every assembly/step, forces the 0 mode real (field.cpp:1196-1200 "// make 0 mode real ... cdata[cc][1] = 0.0;"), and a dedicated impose_zero_mode() utility exists (field.hpp:274-281, zeroing the mode's 2*ncomp reals; wrapped by vorticity_equation::impose_zero_modes(), vorticity_equation.cpp:36-42). (4) Nothing feeds the mode: the random IC fills amplitudes only "if (k2 > 0)" (field.cpp:2445), and every forcing band test excludes it, e.g. vorticity_equation.cpp:360-363 "if ((k2 > 0) && (this->fk0 <= knorm) && (this->fk1 >= knorm))". TurTLE's mainline solvers carry no passive scalar, so it exhibits no scalar-mean practice; the velocity mechanism is the transferable one. Net effect: the mean starts exactly zero and is re-zeroed multiple times per step, so no roundoff/aliasing residual of the nonlinear term can ever accumulate there — the exact failure our trigger bug exhibited, now pinned on our side at the RHS (src/Generator.jl:416-418, applied at 479 and 632).

items.concern: The κ=0 (mean) velocity mode: neither conserved nor damped by the dynamics
items.reference_practice: GHOST pins the mean velocity to zero at every RK substep, at state level: the update loop runs only where the mask holds — include/hd_rkstep2.f90:18 "IF ((kn2(k,j,i).le.kmax).and.(kn2(k,j,i).ge.tiny)) THEN" — and every mode outside it, κ=0 included, is hard-zeroed each substep (lines 26–28 "vx(k,j,i) = 0.0_GP" etc.). The lower gate `tiny = min(1e-5, .1/nmax²)` is set at main3D.fpp:1736 under the comment "tiny: minimum truncation for dealiasing" (line 1725). The pin is unconditional — even a forcing with a mean component could not accumulate one.
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:405–418: "The κ = 0 (mean) mode of the assembled advective term is pinned to zero EXACTLY … Every reference DNS pins this mode" — `_zero_mean_mode!` (line 416) zeroes the [1,1,1] modes, applied inside `velocity_rhs!` at Generator.jl:475 between the nonlinear assembly and the forcing source. Mechanism differs from GHOST: we pin the RHS's mean (conserving ⟨u⟩, normally zero from the seed — State.jl:121–125 zeroes the envelope at κ=0) rather than zeroing the state, deliberately so "a forcing that deliberately drives a mean remains expressible" (Generator.jl:412–413). A caller who does force the mean gets no damping (ℰ = exp(0) = 1), which GHOST's state-pin makes impossible.
items.consequence_if_missing: The discrete ⟨u×ω⟩ residual (roundoff-level per step) integrates undamped and grows at the Lyapunov rate — measured in this code at 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps — silently adding a uniform sweep that inflates u′, the CFL speed, and every tracer trajectory.

items.concern: The κ=0 (mean) scalar mode: conserved, not zeroed
items.reference_practice: GHOST treats the scalar mean differently from the velocity mean — it is frozen, not zeroed: include/phd_rkstep2.f90:37–41 "ELSE IF (kn2(k,j,i).lt.tiny) THEN … th(k,j,i) = C20(k,j,i)" (C20 is the scalar's start-of-substep copy), while the same branch zeroes vx,vy,vz. The scalar mean is a conserved quantity of advection–diffusion and GHOST enforces exactly that.
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:586 (scalar_rhs! docstring): the divergence "form conserves the scalar mean exactly: the divergence has no κ=0" content — plus the same `_zero_mean_mode!(N̂)` pin at Generator.jl:624 killing the roundoff residual of the discrete divergence; the seed is mean-zero by construction (State.jl:210–212, envelope zeroed at κ=0, "that mode's coefficient IS the spatial mean").
items.consequence_if_missing: A drifting scalar mean corrupts `scalar_variance` (documented "for a mean-zero φ", src/Observables.jl:203) and every variance-targeting forcing (VarianceRescaling, VarianceController) then chases a target contaminated by the square of the mean.

items.concern: The pressure/Leray projection's division by |κ|² at κ=0
items.reference_practice: GHOST never evaluates the 0/0: nonlhd3 special-cases, for each output component, the whole plane where that component's own wavenumber vanishes — pseudospec3D_hd.f90:439 "g(k,j,1) = -a(k,j,1)" for the kx=0 plane of the x-component (no /kk2 term at all), the general formula "…+kx(i)*(…)/kk2(k,j,i)" (line 448) running only from i=2; likewise j=1 for y (line ~473) and k=1 for z (line ~497).
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:519–520 delegates to PF's `helmholtz_projection!`; the backend guards the mode explicitly (inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/DifferentialOperators.jl:207–209: "longitudinal = (…) / ifelse(iszero(squared), one(squared), squared)" — ℙ acts as identity at κ=0), and our own comment states the consequence we rely on: "the Leray projection legitimately keeps constants (ℙ(0) = I)" (src/Generator.jl:408–409).
items.consequence_if_missing: A 0/0 at the mean mode produces NaN in the projected nonlinear term on the first step; the NaN propagates to every mode through the next transform pair and the run dies (or, worse, Float32 flushes it to garbage that survives).

items.concern: Nyquist (unpaired even-N rfft) mode: inside or outside the dealias mask
items.reference_practice: GHOST's spherical mask ends far below Nyquist: main3D.fpp:1727+1731 "kmax = 1.0/9.0 … kmax = kmax*real(nx)**2" — i.e. κ² ≤ (N/3)², so the ±N/2 planes are outside and are hard-zeroed at every substep by the `kn2 ≤ kmax` gate (include/hd_rkstep2.f90:18); the Nyquist mode never carries signal and its unpaired-mode pathologies never arise.
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationDomain.jl:157–161 `_retained_nyquist_fraction`: 2/3 (TwoThirds) and 2√2/3 ≈ 0.94 (PhaseShift) — both < 1, so the sharp masks built by `_build_dealias` (lines 259–261, spherical `spectral_cutoff` at `_cutoff_wavenumber`) exclude the Nyquist plane; HouLi alone keeps it but by construction damps it "to that precision's machine epsilon" via strength = -log(eps(T)) (SimulationDomain.jl:96–99 and 263–270). PhaseShift's docstring additionally records the half-cell-shift Nyquist caveat and why the cutoff makes it moot (SimulationDomain.jl:146–150).
items.consequence_if_missing: Energy aliases onto the unpaired Nyquist mode, which has no conjugate partner to keep the physical field real under generic spectral manipulation, and the 2/3-rule's exactness claim fails at the band edge.

items.concern: Where dealiasing is enforced: on the state every substep, or on the assembled term only
items.reference_practice: GHOST enforces the band on the STATE inside every RK substep — the update loop's ELSE branch zeroes vx,vy,vz wherever kn2 > kmax (include/hd_rkstep2.f90:18–28) — so out-of-band content can never persist regardless of its source (a restart file, a hand-written IC, roundoff), because the invariant is re-imposed 3× per step.
items.our_evidence: We truncate the ASSEMBLED term (the dealias kernel folded into the projection pass, src/Generator.jl:481–486) and the seed (src/State.jl:140 "convolve!(û, û, convolve(envelope, domain.dealias))"), never the state: band-limitedness holds by induction — the IF update û ← ℰ(û + b·hu) (src/Propagator.jl:307–309) is per-mode, so out-of-band modes that start zero stay zero exactly.
items.consequence_if_missing: Nothing in a normal run; but content written out-of-band by an out-of-band writer (a hand edit of `state.velocity_spectral`, a future forcing that skips the band) persists — decaying only viscously — and no runtime check enforces the invariant the induction assumes.

items.concern: Hermitian (conjugate) symmetry of random initial conditions and stochastic forcing
items.reference_practice: GHOST builds random spectral data with explicit conjugate mirroring on the self-conjugate kx=0 plane — examples/initialfv.f90_random:19–24: "C1(1,j,1) = (COS(phase)+im*SIN(phase))*dump; C1(1,ny-j+2,1) = conjg(C1(1,j,1))" with "C1(1,1,1) = 0." (line 18) — and its phaseshift subroutine multiplies half that plane by cdump and the mirror half by conjg(cdump), with the comment that the planes "must be dealt with care to keep the Fourier transform of 'a' real" (pseudospec3D_hd.f90:2088–2092, 2110–2124).
items.our_evidence: Present by construction — the failure is unrepresentable: every random field is drawn in PHYSICAL space and carried to spectral by the r2c transform, which produces exact Hermitian symmetry. Velocity/scalar seeds: src/State.jl:113–114 "copyto!(field_data(noise), randn(rng, T, …)); to_spectral!(û, noise, domain.velocity_plans)"; the OU forcing noise likewise: src/Forcing.jl:747–748 "randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical)); to_spectral!(noise_spectral, noise_physical, plans)". All subsequent spectral operations are per-mode multiplications by real radial symbols or r2c products, which preserve the symmetry exactly — no code path writes half-planes by hand.
items.consequence_if_missing: A symmetry-broken spectral field has a complex inverse transform; the c2r silently discards the imaginary part, so energy leaks and every quadratic diagnostic is wrong with no error raised.

items.concern: rfft half-spectrum Parseval weighting (factor 2 vs 1) in energy reductions
items.reference_practice: GHOST weights the folded axis explicitly in every reduction: energy counts the kx=0 plane once and every i ≥ 2 plane twice — pseudospec3D_hd.f90:556–563: the ista=1 plane accumulates "(abs(a)**2+…)*tmp" and the i=2,iend loop "2*(abs(a)**2+…)*tmp"; the same 1-vs-2 split runs through spectrumc, hdcheck's divergence sum, and helicity.
items.our_evidence: src/Observables.jl:76 "kinetic_energy(u) = inner(u, u) / 2" delegates to PF's `inner`, which applies the weighting exactly — including the case GHOST elides: inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/Reductions.jl:828–832: each mode counts "twice — except the folded axis's zero plane and — when it is even — its Nyquist plane, which count once (decision 41)". (GHOST's uniform factor 2 for i ≥ 2 would double-count a populated Nyquist plane; benign there only because its mask keeps that plane empty.)
items.consequence_if_missing: Every energy, dissipation, and variance is wrong by up to a factor ~2 (or subtly wrong at the folded planes) — silently, since the totals still look plausible.

items.concern: Energy-spectrum shell binning: the κ=0 shell and the first/last shell edges
items.reference_practice: GHOST bins round-to-nearest with a boundary nudge and drops the mean mode: pseudospec3D_hd.f90:1249–1250 "kmn = int(sqrt(kk2(k,j,1))/Dkk+.501); IF ((kmn.gt.0).and.(kmn.le.nmax/2+1))" — shell m collects |κ| within ±Δκ/2 of mΔκ, κ=0 is excluded by kmn>0, and the shell list caps at nmax/2+1. Output is a density, E(κ)=½Ek/Dkk at abscissa Dkk·i (lines 1160–1163).
items.our_evidence: src/Observables.jl:328 delegates to PF `radial_spectrum`: same round-to-nearest centred shells (PF Reductions.jl: "shell m collects |k| within ±Δκ/2 of mΔκ", ties-to-even documented), but the κ=0 shell is KEPT (shells run from 0) so the sum exactly refines `inner`, and the return is a per-shell ENERGY, not a density — the distinction is documented against the Phenomenology density convention (src/Observables.jl:346–352: "the two differ by the shell width Δκ = 2π/L and are not interchangeable"). The one consumer for which the κ=0 shell would be poison guards it explicitly: `integral_scale` excludes it in both sums and throws on an energy-free field (src/Observables.jl:373–384).
items.consequence_if_missing: A mean-mode contribution silently biases the lowest shell (exactly where the integral-scale ratio weights most), and a first/last-shell edge convention mismatch corrupts comparisons against reference spectra.

items.concern: CFL and viscous-stability handling
items.reference_practice: GHOST runs a FIXED dt read from parameter.inp (main3D.fpp:459 NAMELIST "parameter / dt,step,…", with only a uniform mult refinement at line 865 "dt = dt/real(mult)"); its viscous term is explicit inside RK (include/hd_rkstep2.f90:21 "dt*(nu*vx(k,j,i)+…)"), so stability is entirely the user's dt choice, and the safeguard is monitoring: include/hd_global.f90 writes max|ω| to maximum.txt every cstep ("CALL maxabs(vx,vy,vz,rmp,0)") for the user to judge the Courant number offline.
items.our_evidence: Stronger than the reference on both halves. Advective: adaptive Δt = min(advective CFL, resolution bound, max_dt) — src/SimulationRun.jl:514–520 "advective = speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : …; resolution = 1 / (diffusivity * κ_min^2); return min(advective, resolution, sim.max_dt)" — with the per-scheme ceiling scaled by the dealias band (src/Propagator.jl:605–612, `_base_cfl` per scheme, no silent fallback). Viscous: exact by the integrating factor, so no viscous stability limit exists at all (src/Generator.jl:6–8). Blow-up monitoring is in-loop, not offline: non-finite velocity AND scalar guards after every step (src/SimulationRun.jl:579–588).
items.consequence_if_missing: A dt chosen once and outgrown by the flow (or a decaying flow's runaway adaptive step) blows the run up or freezes it — both failure modes are documented and guarded in cfl_timestep's comment block (SimulationRun.jl:483–512).

items.concern: Always-on conservation/balance ledger (energy, enstrophy, injection; divergence drift)
items.reference_practice: GHOST writes an unconditional running ledger: hdcheck (pseudospec3D_hd.f90:984–1105) appends time, ⟨v²⟩, ⟨ω²⟩ and the injection rate to balance.txt every cstep ("OPEN(1,file='balance.txt',position='append')"), with an optional ⟨(∇·v)²⟩ divergence check (chk=1) and the scalar twin pscheck → scalar.txt (pseudospec3D_phd.f90:286–332); the HD solver calls it every cstep from include/hd_global.f90:3.
items.our_evidence: Every ledger ingredient exists as an observable — `kinetic_energy`, `dissipation`, `scalar_variance`, injection via `flow_parameters` (src/SimulationRun.jl:440–448) — but nothing records them unless asked: the run layer's contract is "the callback *is* the observation" (src/SimulationRun.jl:23), and accumulating statistics is the caller's analysis by the package's own scope statement (CLAUDE.md/module docstrings). Solenoidality is exact by construction (PF's ℙ "exactly annihilates the discrete divergence at every mode", PF DifferentialOperators.jl:197–199), so GHOST's optional divergence monitor has no drift to catch here.
items.consequence_if_missing: A slow budget drift (forcing bug, integrator defect) that a default balance file would expose in one glance goes unnoticed in any run whose caller did not wire a callback for it.

items.concern: Restart / exact continuation (fields, forcing state, schedule counters)
items.reference_practice: GHOST restarts a run bit-consistently from binary output: main3D.fpp:2145–2176 — "IF stat.ne.0 a previous run is continued": fields re-read (io_read of vx,vy,vz then r2c), the forcing schedule counter rebuilt in phase ("timef = int(modulo(float(ini-1),float(fstep)))", line 2156), and for the slowly-varying forcing (rand=2) the fxnew/fxold target arrays are themselves written and re-read so the forcing resumes mid-ramp (lines 2175+).
items.our_evidence: Searched src/ for restart|checkpoint|io_write|serialize|save: the only hit is `Particles.restart!` (src/Particles.jl:247), a particle-scheme history reset, not a run continuation. No field I/O, no checkpoint format, no RNG-state capture contract exists (StochasticOU holds its MersenneTwister in-struct, src/Forcing.jl:727; seeding uses Random.default_rng(), src/SimulationRun.jl:292). A caller can Serialization.serialize a whole Simulation, but nothing promises that round-trips exactly (GPU arrays, transform plans).
items.consequence_if_missing: A long production run cannot survive a crash or a queue limit without replaying from t=0, and a stochastic-forcing run cannot be continued reproducibly — the OU state and its RNG stream are lost with the process.

items.concern: Parameter / configuration compatibility validation before the run
items.reference_practice: GHOST validates before integrating: main3D.fpp:1719 "INCLUDE SOLVERCHECK_" under the comment "we verify that all parameters and compilation options are compatible with the SOLVER being used" (per-solver *_validate.f90 files), and IC/forcing files STOP on incompatible geometry — initialfv.f90:17–21: "IF ( abs(Lx-Ly).gt.tiny ) … PRINT *,'TG forcing require at least Lx=Ly'; STOP".
items.our_evidence: Constructor-time guards throughout: cfl > 0 and max_dt > 0 with physical explanations (src/SimulationRun.jl:302–306), forcing-parameter checks (src/Forcing.jl:370–377 VarianceRescaling, 563–578 VarianceController, 719–724 StochasticOU), timestep positivity on both adaptive and fixed routes (src/SimulationRun.jl:549–551), and a physics-level compatibility warning the reference has no analogue of — the scalar under-resolution warning when κ_max·η_B falls below the well-resolved floor (src/SimulationRun.jl:360–366: "will measure a truncated field. Raise κ_max_η by √Sc…").
items.consequence_if_missing: A mis-specified run burns its whole budget before the incompatibility surfaces as a blow-up or a silently truncated measurement.

lanes.mean_mode: GHOST handles κ=0 at STATE level, inside every RK substep, with different rules for velocity and scalar. The update loop runs only inside the band gate — include/hd_rkstep2.f90:18: "IF ((kn2(k,j,i).le.kmax).and.(kn2(k,j,i).ge.tiny)) THEN" — where `tiny = min(1e-5_GP, .1_GP/(real(nmax)**2))` (main3D.fpp:1736, commented "tiny: minimum truncation for dealiasing" at line 1725) is a strictly-positive floor that only the κ=0 mode falls below. VELOCITY: every mode outside the gate, the mean included, is hard-zeroed each substep — hd_rkstep2.f90:26–28 "vx(k,j,i) = 0.0_GP; vy(k,j,i) = 0.0_GP; vz(k,j,i) = 0.0_GP" — an unconditional pin of ⟨u⟩ = 0 three times per step, immune to roundoff accumulation and to any forcing with a spurious mean. SCALAR: the mean is CONSERVED, not zeroed — the passive-scalar solver splits the ELSE into two branches, include/phd_rkstep2.f90:37–41: "ELSE IF (kn2(k,j,i).lt.tiny) THEN … th(k,j,i) = C20(k,j,i)" (C20 holds the start-of-substep scalar), freezing ⟨φ⟩ at its initial value while still zeroing the velocity mean in the same branch. Complementarily, the Leray projection never divides at κ=0: nonlhd3 special-cases, per output component, the whole plane where that component's wavenumber vanishes — pseudospec3D_hd.f90:439 "g(k,j,1) = -a(k,j,1)" (no /kk2 term on the kx=0 plane for the x-component; the divided formula at line 448 starts at i=2) — so the 0/0 is never evaluated rather than being guarded by an epsilon. Random forcings zero the mean explicitly at generation (examples/initialfv.f90_random:18 "C1(1,1,1) = 0.").

items.concern: Conservation of the κ=0 (mean) velocity mode — the trigger concern
items.reference_practice: hit3d makes the mean mode's RHS identically zero by construction: the divergence-form convective term carries an explicit wavenumber factor on every term — rhs_velocity.f90:89–94 "t1(1) = - ( akx(i) * wrk(i,j,k,1) + aky(k) * wrk(i,j,k,2) + akz(j) * wrk(i,j,k,3) )" and "t1(4) = - nu * ( akx(i)**2 + aky(k)**2 + akz(j)**2 )" — so at k=0 (akx=aky=akz=0) both convection and diffusion vanish exactly. The IC zeroes shell 0 (init_velocity.f90:130–142 "if (n_shell .gt. 0 .and. n_shell .le. kmax) … else wrk(i:i+1,j,k,4:6) = zip") and the forcing books only n_shell>0 nodes (m_force.f90:41). The mean is conserved at exactly zero with no damping needed.
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:405–418 (uncommitted working-tree fix, landed during this audit — the concern WAS absent, confirmed as the trigger): "# The κ = 0 (mean) mode of the assembled advective term is pinned to zero EXACTLY. … the residual is integrated undamped and, the flow being chaotic, grows at the Lyapunov rate: measured 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps." `_zero_mean_mode!(N̂)` is wired between nonlinear assembly and forcing source at Generator.jl:480 (velocity) — our rotational form needs the explicit pin because ⟨u×ω⟩=0 holds only to roundoff discretely, unlike hit3d's structural i·k zero.
items.consequence_if_missing: The roundoff residual of ⟨u×ω⟩ passes the Leray projection unchanged (identity at k=0), meets integrating factor exp(0)=1, and integrates undamped: a spurious uniform mean flow grows at the Lyapunov rate (measured 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps), Galilean-drifting every tracer and inflating u′ and the CFL speed.

items.concern: Conservation of the κ=0 mean of the passive scalar
items.reference_practice: Structural, as for velocity: every convective term in rhs_scalars.f90:110–116 carries akx/aky/akz factors, zero at k=0. Additionally the physical-space scalar ICs zero the mean coefficient by hand — init_scalars.f90:350–351: "! making sure that the mean is ero" / "if (iammaster) fields(1,1,1,3+n_scalar) = zip" (also :323), and the double-delta construction re-zeroes n_shell==0 after its sign() step re-introduces a mean (init_scalars.f90:255).
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:625–633: the conservative form −∇·(uφ) has no κ=0 component (docstring: "The conservative form conserves the scalar mean exactly: the divergence has no κ=0 component"), now belt-and-braces pinned by `_zero_mean_mode!(N̂)` at Generator.jl:633; the seeder zeroes the mode at IC — src/State.jl:210–212: "The envelope vanishes at κ = 0, which IS the mean removal".
items.consequence_if_missing: A drifting ⟨φ⟩ offsets every scalar moment; with variance-holding forcings normalizing against ⟨φ²⟩ the mean would silently absorb part of the held budget.

items.concern: Leray/pressure projection's division at k=0
items.reference_practice: pressure.f90:28–29 substitutes a huge benign denominator before dividing: "if (lapl1.eq.0.d0) lapl1 = 9e20" / "if (lapl2.eq.0.d0) lapl2 = 9e20", so p(k=0) ≈ 0 and the mean velocity passes through the pressure correction unchanged.
items.our_evidence: Reached from src/Generator.jl:523–524 (`helmholtz_projection!(out, product_spectral, domain.multipliers, …)`); the guard lives in the PF backend (inspiration clone DifferentialOperators.jl:267–268: `ifelse(iszero(squared), one(squared), squared)`), documented as "the zero Fourier mode left unchanged" — ℙ is the identity at k=0. Note this identity convention is exactly why item 1 needed the explicit pin in rotational form.
items.consequence_if_missing: 0/0 at the first mode NaNs the projected term and poisons the whole field within one step — immediate, total blow-up.

items.concern: Nyquist (oddball) mode treatment and where the Nyquist plane sits relative to the dealias mask
items.reference_practice: hit3d's cubical mask purges every mode with any |k_i| > N/3 on every RHS assembly — ialias built at x_fftw.f90:302–311 ("ialias is just the number of wavenumbers at (i,j,k) that have their magnitude higher than nx/3"), applied at rhs_velocity.f90:121–123 ("wrk(i,j,k,1:3) = zip") — and N/2 > N/3, so the unpaired Nyquist plane is always inside the purge and never carries signal; the spectrum loops also stop at i = nx, skipping the kx-Nyquist plane entirely (m_stats.f90:215).
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationDomain.jl:265–269: the spherical cutoff `T(_retained_nyquist_fraction(strategy)) * T(N / 2) * T(2π / L)` sits strictly below Nyquist for TwoThirds (2/3) and PhaseShift (2√2/3 ≈ 0.94); HouLi keeps Nyquist but damps it to machine epsilon by default (SimulationDomain.jl:85–89 and 274–278). The oddball-derivative hazard is handled in the PF backend: the first-derivative wavenumber is zeroed at the Nyquist mode "so that derivatives of real fields stay real" while the squared family keeps the true k² (PF clone Fields.jl:1433, 1450–1451).
items.consequence_if_missing: A live unpaired Nyquist mode makes odd spectral derivatives complex-leak into real fields and accumulates un-dealiased energy at the band edge — slow contamination or sawtooth instability.

items.concern: Hermitian symmetry of random initial conditions and stochastic forcing
items.reference_practice: hit3d never touches spectral coefficients directly for random data: Gaussian noise is generated in physical space and pushed through the r2c FFT, so conjugate symmetry holds by construction — init_velocity.f90:113–119: "wrk(:,:,:,1:3) = sqrt(-two*log(…)) * sin(TWO_PI*…)" then "call xFFT3d(1,n)"; the spectrum shaping then multiplies modes by real radial factors only, which preserves the symmetry.
items.our_evidence: Same mechanism: src/State.jl:112–114 fills a physical field with `randn` and calls `to_spectral!`; src/Forcing.jl:745–750 (StochasticOU) does `randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical)); to_spectral!(…)` — docstring at Forcing.jl:680–682: "generated as a real physical field, transformed, and band-limited — guaranteeing a valid real field with no Hermitian-symmetry bookkeeping".
items.consequence_if_missing: A non-Hermitian seed or forcing puts imaginary garbage in physical space; the c2r transform silently discards or aliases it, so the run computes on a field that is not the one the statistics assume.

items.concern: The initial condition confined to the dealiased band before the first step
items.reference_practice: hit3d truncates the state once at startup — main.f90:75–76: "! need to dealias the fields at the beginning / if (task.eq.'hydro') call dealias_all" — and init_scalars.f90:30–36 purges every scalar mode with ialias > 0 right after generation, so no out-of-band content enters the first nonlinear product.
items.our_evidence: src/State.jl:140: `convolve!(û, û, convolve(envelope, domain.dealias))` — the dealias truncation is composed into the seeding envelope itself (comment: "The truncation rides in the envelope rather than as a second sweep"); scalar twin at State.jl:223 ("truncation folded in, as for the velocity").
items.consequence_if_missing: Out-of-band IC content is never fed by the band-limited RHS but decays only viscously, polluting early spectra and the first nonlinear products under HouLi where the mask does not remove it.

items.concern: Energy-spectrum shell binning: first/last shell conventions and the r2c conjugate-pair weight
items.reference_practice: hit3d bins by n_shell = nint(|k|) over shells 1..kmax only, half-weights the kx=0 plane for the missing conjugates — m_stats.f90:222: "if (akx(i).eq.0.d0) fac2 = 0.5d0 * fac2" — skips the kx-Nyquist plane (loop to nx), clamps the first shell's inner radius (velocity_rescale.f90:88: "if (k.eq.1) sc_rad2 = 0.d0") and doubles the scalar spectrum back (m_stats.f90:419–420: "multiplying by two because we summed only half").
items.our_evidence: src/Observables.jl:327–329 delegates to PF's `radial_spectrum` and halves it; the backend bins ALL modes into shells 0..corner with exact per-mode Parseval weights so the shell total equals `inner` exactly (PF clone Reductions.jl:1183: "Shells run from 0 to the corner wavenumber, so the sum covers *all* modes (an exact `inner` refinement)"), with a documented ties-to-even boundary convention; the κ=0 shell is excluded where it must be — src/Observables.jl:379–380: `sum(broadcast((k, e) -> k > 0 ? e : zero(e), κ, E))`.
items.consequence_if_missing: Wrong conjugate weighting or shell edges skews E(κ) at the first shells — exactly where the integral scale and model-spectrum fits weight most — and makes Σ E_n ≠ k, a broken diagnostic invariant.

items.concern: Forcing normalization over a near-empty band (division by the band's own energy)
items.reference_practice: hit3d itself does NOT guard it: m_force.f90:161 "fac = FAMP / energy" divides by the summed band energy with no floor or emptiness test — an unbounded kick if the band is empty. The guard practice comes from TurTLE (cited in our source): substitute a benign denominator below a machine-epsilon-relative floor.
items.our_evidence: src/Forcing.jl:89: `_band_is_empty(band_value) = !(isfinite(band_value) && band_value > zero(band_value))` — a scale-free positivity test (the comment explains why no constant floor: it would break the scalar equation's exact scaling symmetry); applied at Forcing.jl:385 (VarianceRescaling: "nothing in the band yet"), :618 (VarianceController), :643–645 (ConstantPower, with the TurTLE citation "if (energy_in_shell < 10*eps) energy_in_shell = 1"), and the OU noise-variance guard at :757.
items.consequence_if_missing: A band emptied by seeding or by a :total rescale receives an unbounded (or NaN) amplitude on the next step — instant blow-up from the forcing itself, as hit3d's own unguarded division would.

items.concern: Adaptive-timestep control: per-step Courant measurement, change limiting, and a hard ceiling
items.reference_practice: hit3d measures the Courant number every step from the componentwise speed — rhs_velocity.f90:31–38: "wrk(:,:,:,4) = abs(wrk(…,1)) + abs(wrk(…,2)) + abs(wrk(…,3))" … "courant = courant * dt / dx" — and my_dt.f90:14–19 nudges dt multiplicatively with a growth limiter and a hard cap: "if (courant.lt.courant_max) then DT = DT * 1.01d0; DT = min(DT,0.01) else DT = DT/1.05d0".
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationRun.jl:480–520: `cfl_timestep` takes the minimum of the advective step (Δt = C·Δx/u_max from the cache's deposited max_speed), a derived resolution bound `1/(D·κ_min²)` that stops the decaying-flow runaway, and the caller's `max_dt`; the ceiling C itself is derived from the scheme's imaginary-axis stability limit and rescaled by the retained dealias band (src/Propagator.jl:605–611). The choice NOT to use hit3d's limiter is recorded in-code: "hit3d nudges Δt multiplicatively with a 1% growth limiter and a hard min(DT, 0.01) … this route was taken instead because it needs no constant at all" (SimulationRun.jl, cfl_timestep comment). The L2 speed is consistent with our spherical mask (|u·κ| ≤ |u|κ_max is sharp), where hit3d's L1 speed matches its cubical mask.
items.consequence_if_missing: An unbounded adaptive step diverges as a decaying flow approaches rest (our comment records Δt reaching ~1e15, the integrating factor then annihilating every mode), or an unlimited upward jump after a lull overshoots the stability region.

items.concern: Viscous/diffusive stability, including the Schmidt-number scaling of the scalar's limit
items.reference_practice: hit3d advances diffusion explicitly (AB2), so it must bound dt by the diffusive limit: my_dt.f90:22–30 — "make sure DT is appropriate for scalars / DT < 0.09 * dx^2*Pe" and "DT = min(DT,DT*courant_max/courant/sc(n))" — tightening the step for every scalar with Sc > … plus the hard cap min(DT, 0.01).
items.our_evidence: The diffusive stability limit does not exist for us: viscosity and diffusivity are advanced exactly by the integrating factor — src/Generator.jl velocity_integrating_factor docstring: "advances its viscous (and linear-forcing) part exactly — machine-exact, with no stability restriction"; the scalar's faster diffusivity still enters the timestep through the resolution bound — src/SimulationRun.jl:513–515: `diffusivity = … max(conditions.viscosity, conditions.viscosity / conditions.schmidt)` — as an accuracy bound, not a stability one.
items.consequence_if_missing: For an explicit-diffusion code, a step above the diffusive limit is a hard blow-up at the highest wavenumbers; for us the exact factor removes the failure mode entirely, which must be (and is) compensated by the accuracy-motivated resolution bound.

items.concern: Checkpoint/restart of a long run (state + clock + timestep), with a defined post-restart protocol
items.reference_practice: hit3d writes a parallel MPI-IO restart file carrying the spectral fields plus TIME and DT (restart_io.f90:297: "call MPI_FILE_WRITE(fh, DT, count, MPI_REAL8, …)"; read back at :379: "read(91) nx1, ny1, nz1, nums1, nles1, TIME, DT") and defines a degraded-order restart: the AB2 history is not saved, so the first step is Euler with dt halved — begin_restart.f90:27–38: "After the restart, the first timestep is done using a simple Euler scheme … we need to start with the timestep which is smaller than the last" (dt = half * dt). Its IC RNG is wall-clock seeded (init_velocity.f90:55–58), so the guarded invariant is resumability, not bit-reproducibility.
items.our_evidence: Searched src/ for restart, checkpoint, serialize, save/load, HDF5, JLD, MPI/file writes of the state: the only hit is Particles' `restart!` (Particles.jl:247), which resets a trajectory scheme's multistep history — no checkpoint of the spectral state, clock, forcing state, or RNG stream exists anywhere. Fresh-run reproducibility IS present (State.jl:110 `rng` keyword; Forcing.jl StochasticOU `seed = 0` "fixes the random stream, so a forced run is reproducible"), but a crashed or wall-clock-limited run cannot resume.
items.consequence_if_missing: Any interruption loses the entire run — at production resolutions that is days of GPU time — and no statistically-converged long run can be split across job allocations; our RK schemes are self-starting, so unlike hit3d only the state, clock, forcing internal state, and RNG position would need saving.

items.concern: Out-of-band state mutation invalidates dependent history and cached values
items.reference_practice: After the mid-run spectral rescale mutates the fields outside the dynamics, hit3d discards the multistep history that no longer describes the state — main.f90:116–118: "call velocity_rescale / ! after rescaling, the time-sceping needs to be first order / fov = .true.; fos = .true." — forcing the next step to Euler rather than combining an AB2 pair across the discontinuity.
items.our_evidence: The same invariant, generalized: src/Cache.jl:364 `fields_modified!` advances the fields epoch so every cached observable read throws rather than serving a stale value after an announced mutation; src/Particles.jl:247/505 `restart!` "discards a scheme's history after an out-of-band reposition" (`buffers.cache.history_filled = 0` for AdamsBashforth). The field integrators are single-step RK, so they carry no history to poison.
items.consequence_if_missing: A multistep combination or a cached diagnostic straddling the mutation silently mixes two inconsistent states — first-order-wrong dynamics or wrong reported observables with nothing failing.

lanes.mean_mode: hit3d never damps the mean mode — it guarantees the mean's RHS is identically zero, starts it at zero, and excludes shell 0 from every intervention. Four mechanisms: (1) STRUCTURAL RHS ZERO: the divergence-form convective term carries an explicit wavenumber factor on every term — rhs_velocity.f90:89–94: "t1(1) = - ( akx(i) * wrk(i,j,k,1) + aky(k) * wrk(i,j,k,2) + akz(j) * wrk(i,j,k,3) )" and "t1(4) = - nu * ( akx(i)**2 + aky(k)**2 + akz(j)**2 )" — at k=0 all of akx, aky, akz vanish, so convection AND diffusion of the mean are exactly zero; identically for the scalar (rhs_scalars.f90:110–116). (2) PRESSURE GUARD: the k=0 division in the pressure solve is defused by a huge denominator — pressure.f90:28–29: "if (lapl1.eq.0.d0) lapl1 = 9e20" — so p(0) ≈ 0 and the mean passes through the projection unchanged. (3) IC AND RESCALE EXCLUDE SHELL 0: init_velocity.f90:130–142 gates on "if (n_shell .gt. 0 .and. n_shell .le. kmax)" else "wrk(i:i+1,j,k,4:6) = zip"; velocity_rescale.f90:141–146 zeroes every mode outside shells 1..kmax including the mean; physical-space scalar ICs zero the mean coefficient by hand — init_scalars.f90:350–351: "! making sure that the mean is ero" / "if (iammaster) fields(1,1,1,3+n_scalar) = zip". (4) FORCING EXCLUDES SHELL 0: only nodes with "n_shell .gt. 0 .and. n_shell .le. kfmax" are booked as forced (m_force.f90:41). Net: mean velocity and scalar are conserved at exactly zero for the whole run — by structure of the divergence form, not by damping. This is precisely the guarantee our rotational form lacked: ℙ(u×ω) at k=0 is ⟨u×ω⟩, zero only analytically, and PF's projection is deliberately the identity there — which is why our fix (landed in the working tree during this audit as Generator.jl's `_zero_mean_mode!`, pinning the advective term's κ=0 mode between assembly and forcing source) is the explicit counterpart of hit3d's structural zero.

Fluidsim keeps the k=0 velocity/scalar mode EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION rather than pinning it per step. (1) Initial conditions zero it explicitly: solvers/ns3d/init_fields.py:129-131 "if mpi.rank == 0: field_fft[0, 0, 0] = 0.0" (each scalar-like field of the noise IC) and :173 "vv_fft[ii][0, 0, 0] = 0.0" in compute_solenoidal_noise_fft, before the Leray projection and dealiasing. (2) Forcing can never reach it: the forced set is K in [kmin_forcing, kmax_forcing] with default nkmin_forcing=4 (base/forcing/base.py:192 '{"nkmax_forcing": 5, "nkmin_forcing": 4}'; base/forcing/specific.py:278 "COND_NO_F = np.logical_or(K > self.kmax_forcing, K < self.kmin_forcing)"), so k=0 (K=0 < kmin) is always in COND_NO_F and zeroed (specific.py:775 "f_fft[self.COND_NO_F] = 0.0"). (3) The projection is the identity there via an epsilon floor, never a 0/0: operators/operators3d.py:292-294 "K2_not0 = np.copy(self.K2); ... K2_not0[0, 0, 0] = 1e-14" and the recurring idiom :771-773 "K_square_nozero[K_square_nozero == 0] = 1e-14". (4) When hypo-viscosity is on, the k=0 mode is explicitly DAMPED by a special case rather than divided by zero: base/solvers/pseudo_spect.py:176-186 "f_d_hypo = self.params.nu_m4 / self.oper.K2_not0**2  # mode K2 = 0 !  ... f_d_hypo[0, 0, 0] = f_d_hypo[0, 0, 1]" — the mean mode inherits the first mode's damping rate. (5) There is NO per-step zeroing of the k=0 nonlinear tendency: tendencies are projected and dealiased (solver.py:242-244), but neither touches k=0; with the default 2/3 cubic mask no aliases fold onto k=0, so the residual is roundoff-only, and it is left undamped unless nu_m4 is set. An adjacent optional guard exists for the whole kz=0 plane of vz ("no_vz_kz0", solver.py:277-284 dealiasing_variable(vz_fft, self.where_kz_0)) and for the shear modes kh=0 (operators3d.py:268-277 NO_SHEAR_MODES folds "Kx**2 + Ky**2 == 0" into where_dealiased) — both anisotropy-motivated, off by default. OUR side: now stronger than the reference — src/Generator.jl:416-418 `_zero_mean_mode!` pins the assembled advective term's k=0 to exactly zero on every RHS evaluation (velocity at :479, scalar at :632), placed between the nonlinear assembly and the forcing source so a deliberate mean-driving forcing stays expressible; the ICs zero it via the envelope ("The envelope vanishes at κ = 0, which IS the mean removal", src/State.jl:121-127 and :210-214); the OU forcing band starts at (lowest_shell−0.5)·k0 ≥ 0.5·k0 so k=0 is never forced (src/Forcing.jl:266-268).

items.concern: Per-step re-projection and re-dealiasing of the advanced STATE (solenoidality / band-content drift guard)
items.reference_practice: Fluidsim applies the Leray projection and the dealiasing mask to the STATE after every completed time step, not only to the tendencies: solvers/ns3d/time_stepping.py:13-16 "self._time_step_RK(); self.sim.project_state_spect(state_spect); self.sim.oper.dealiasing(state_spect)". This annihilates, every step, the divergence and out-of-band residue that roundoff (or a mis-set forcing) puts into the state.
items.our_evidence: Searched Propagator.jl and SimulationRun.jl for helmholtz_projection/truncate_to_band applied to state.velocity_spectral — none exist; projection and truncation act only inside the tendency assembly (src/Generator.jl:523, :479). The state is advanced by integrating-factor multiplies and stage combinations of projected tendencies only.
items.consequence_if_missing: Divergence residue injected at roundoff each step is damped only by exp(−νκ²Δt), so its steady level is amplified by ~1/(νκ²Δt) at the largest scales — several orders above machine epsilon at low ν, worst in Float32 (the κ=0 extreme of this same series was the trigger bug). Under HouLi, out-of-band content in the state is likewise only damped, never removed. Cheap to guard, silent when it drifts.

items.concern: Advective CFL: norm convention, scheme-dependent coefficient, timestep cap, zero-velocity fallback, dt-change hysteresis
items.reference_practice: Fluidsim bounds dt by the ADDITIVE per-axis bound: base/time_stepping/base.py:364 "tmp = max_ux / self.sim.oper.deltax + max_uy / self.sim.oper.deltay ..." (3-D form :331-336), with a scheme-dependent coefficient (:258-260, CFL=0.4 for RK2/Euler, 1.0 for RK4), a hard cap deltat_max default 0.2 (:42) that is also the zero-velocity fallback (:346-350 "if tmp > 0: deltat_CFL = self.CFL / tmp else: deltat_CFL = self.deltat_max"), and a 2% hysteresis so the materialized exp(−dt·f_lin) arrays are not rebuilt needlessly (:353 "if normalize_diff > 0.02", pseudo_spect.py:151-156).
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationRun.jl:514 "advective = speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : sim.cfl * Δx" uses the Euclidean pointwise maximum (src/Observables.jl:177 "max_speed(u) = maximum(norm, u)") — up to √3 less conservative than the additive bound, compensated by conservative per-scheme bases (src/Propagator.jl:605-606, IFRK2 0.25 / RK3 0.5, vs the imaginary-axis-derived 0.83) scaled by the dealias band (:610-611); the cap is the derived resolution bound min(advective, resolution, max_dt) (SimulationRun.jl:520, with the runaway-Δt derivation at :481-513 explicitly comparing "fluidsim caps at a deltat_max parameter (default 0.2)"); no hysteresis needed since the integrating factor is evaluated lazily per mode, never materialized.

items.concern: Hermitian (conjugate) symmetry of stochastically generated forcing fields

items.concern: Initial-condition hygiene: the seeded state is projected and dealiased before the first step
items.reference_practice: Every ns3d IC path routes through init_state_from_fieldsfft, which Leray-projects the freshly built state (solvers/ns3d/init_fields.py:23-27 "self.sim.state.init_statespect_from(**fields); self.sim.project_state_spect(...)"), and the solenoidal noise builder projects AND dealiases before spectrum shaping (:176-183 "oper.project_perpk3d(*vv_fft); oper.dealiasing(*vv_fft)").
