items.concern: Nyquist / oddball wavenumber treatment (the unpaired mode of even-N real FFTs) in masks and derivative operators
items.reference_practice: Fluidsim removes Nyquist from the dynamics via the mask — default coef_dealiasing 2/3 (operators3d.py:158) and the spherical option "self.K2 >= kmax**2" (operators/base.py:79-82) both exclude it — and explicitly bars it from forcing on the coarse (UNdealiased, coef 1.0, specific.py:241) operator: specific.py:284-288 zeroes the ky/kz Nyquist planes and the last kx index of the forceable set.
items.our_evidence: The two sharp strategies truncate at f·κ_Ny with f = 2/3 or 2√2/3 < 1 (src/SimulationDomain.jl:265-269 `_cutoff_wavenumber`/`spectral_cutoff`), so Nyquist never survives a step; HouLi keeps it but damps to machine epsilon by construction (:275 "strength = T(isnothing(strategy.strength) ? -log(eps(T)) : ...)", docstring: Nyquist multiplied by e^-strength = eps). The unpaired-mode arithmetic itself is the PF backend's contract (clone verified: Fields.jl:1450-1451 zeroes the derivative-family wavenumber at Nyquist so derivatives of real fields stay real, while the squared family keeps true k² for the Laplacian; Parseval weights 1 on the folded axis's zero and Nyquist planes, 2 elsewhere — Reductions.jl radial_spectrum docstring).
items.consequence_if_missing: An unhandled Nyquist mode makes spectral derivatives of real fields complex (an imaginary residue that r2c transforms silently fold into the field), double- or half-counts energy in reductions, and cannot be consistently phase-shifted or forced.

items.concern: The κ=0 velocity mode (mean momentum) must be pinned — it has no viscous damping and no restoring term
items.reference_practice: Rogallo 1981 (NASA TM-81315) formulates homogeneous turbulence in the zero-mean-velocity frame and seeds û(0)=0; Canuto, Hussaini, Quarteroni & Zang, Spectral Methods — Evolution to Complex Geometries (2007), §3.3 Fourier–Galerkin NSE: the k=0 momentum/pressure mode is set aside (the mean flow is a free Galilean parameter, conventionally zero); Pope 2000 §9.1 (DNS in the zero-mean frame). Universal code practice: hard-zero û(0) every step, because the analytic identity ⟨u×ω⟩=0 (Lamb vector = gradient + divergence on a periodic box) holds discretely only to roundoff.
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:405–418 and 480 — landed mid-audit as the fix for this very finding: "The κ = 0 (mean) mode of the assembled advective term is pinned to zero EXACTLY … the residual is integrated undamped and, the flow being chaotic, grows at the Lyapunov rate: measured 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps. Every reference DNS pins this mode."; velocity_rhs! now calls `_zero_mean_mode!(N̂);` (line 480) between the nonlinear assembly and the forcing source, so a forcing that deliberately drives a mean stays expressible.
items.consequence_if_missing: The roundoff residual of the discrete ⟨u×ω⟩ is integrated with exp(0)=1 each step and grows chaotically: a spurious uniform sweep of the whole box (measured 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps) that inflates u′ and the CFL speed, advects every tracer, and biases every Galilean-noninvariant statistic — silently, since nothing goes NaN.

items.concern: The κ=0 scalar mode (scalar mean) must be conserved by the advection term
items.reference_practice: Standard result (Canuto et al. 2007, conservation forms of the advection term; Pope 2000 §12.4 mean-scalar conservation): the conservative form ∇·(uφ) has identically zero spatial mean on a periodic box — its spectral image is iκ·(uφ)^, which vanishes at κ=0 — so a divergence-form pseudospectral scalar conserves ⟨φ⟩ exactly; codes seed ⟨φ⟩=0 and keep it.
items.our_evidence: src/Generator.jl:590–592 (scalar_rhs! docstring): "The conservative form conserves the scalar mean exactly: the divergence has no κ=0 component, and the dealias kernel … leaves that mode untouched"; the roundoff residue is now also pinned — `_zero_mean_mode!(N̂);` at Generator.jl:633. The diffusive integrating factor is exp(−ϰ·0·τ)=1 there (Generator.jl:547–556), and the seeder zeroes the mean (State.jl:210–212: "killing that mode leaves ⟨φ⟩ = 0").
items.consequence_if_missing: ⟨φ⟩ drifts; a nonzero mean leaks into scalar_variance (computed as ⟨φ,φ⟩ assuming mean-zero, Observables.jl:210) and into every mixing diagnostic — wrong diagnostics with no symptom.

items.concern: The Leray/pressure projection's division by |κ|² at κ=0
items.reference_practice: Canuto et al. 2007 §3.3: the pressure Poisson solve |k|²p̂ = ik·N̂ is singular at k=0 (compatibility condition); every spectral code special-cases the k=0 mode of the projector ℙ = I − κκᵀ/|κ|² — skipped in the mode loop or the denominator substituted — since evaluating it naively is 0/0.
items.our_evidence: Our call sites src/Generator.jl:524–525 (`helmholtz_projection!(out, product_spectral, domain.multipliers[, kernel])`); the mechanism is in the PF backend (verified in the study clone, inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/DifferentialOperators.jl:207–208): `longitudinal = (…)/ifelse(iszero(squared), one(squared), squared)` — at κ=0 the denominator becomes 1 and longitudinal 0, so ℙ acts as the identity there, never NaN. The identity-passthrough (ℙ keeps constants, which is mathematically correct) is completed by the RHS mean-mode pinning of Generator.jl:480.
items.consequence_if_missing: 0/0 at the very first projection puts NaN in mode 0; the next inverse transform spreads it to every grid point — instant, total blow-up on step 1.

items.concern: Nyquist (oddball) treatment of the first-derivative multiplier on an even-N real FFT
items.reference_practice: Canuto et al. 2007 §2.1.2 and Trefethen, Spectral Methods in MATLAB, ch. 3: the unpaired Nyquist mode of an even-length real transform has no consistent sign for an odd-order derivative, so the first-derivative wavenumber is set to zero there (derivatives of real fields stay real), while even-order operators (the Laplacian) keep the true k².
items.our_evidence: We build the multipliers at src/SimulationDomain.jl:245 (`multipliers = FieldSpectralMultipliers(velocity_spectral)`); the backend carries exactly the textbook split (PF clone, inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/Fields.jl:1433: "On even-length axes the derivative wavenumber is zeroed at the Nyquist mode (so derivatives of real fields stay real) while the squared wavenumber keeps the true k² (correct Laplacian) — the deliberate Nyquist split"; the zero write at Fields.jl:1450–1451). The projection denominator squares the derivative family, making ℙ exactly idempotent on Nyquist planes too (DifferentialOperators.jl:197–200).
items.consequence_if_missing: Curl, divergence and gradient of real fields acquire spurious imaginary/asymmetric Nyquist content — under HouLi (which retains the Nyquist band) the vorticity, dissipation and the whole rotational-form RHS would be polluted at the grid scale.

items.concern: Dealiasing-mask geometry: is the Nyquist plane inside or outside the retained band
items.reference_practice: Orszag 1971 (J. Atmos. Sci. 28, 1074): sharp 2/3 truncation, Nyquist modes zeroed; Rogallo 1981: phase-shift with spherical truncation at √2N/3, also strictly below Nyquist; Hou & Li 2007: retain to Nyquist but damp it to machine precision with a high-order exponential filter.
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationDomain.jl:144–147: retained fractions 2/3 (TwoThirds), 1 (HouLi), 2√2/3 (PhaseShift); lines 265–269 build the spherical cutoff kernel from one shared expression — both sharp strategies keep κ ≤ f·κ_Ny < κ_Ny, so the Nyquist plane is outside and zeroed. HouLi's default strength is −log(eps(T)) "so the Nyquist mode always damps to that precision's machine epsilon" (lines 84–89, 275). PhaseShift's docstring guards the corner case explicitly (lines 135–139: a half-cell shift cannot translate Nyquist; the spherical cutoff leaves no Nyquist content to mistranslate). The cutoff is computed in ONE element type so a Float32 grid's built band cannot disagree with the advertised κ_max (lines 259–266).
items.consequence_if_missing: Aliased energy at and near the Nyquist plane accumulates uncontrolled — the classic pile-up at the spectrum tail, then blow-up; or a Float32 band silently wider than the κ_max·η criterion the run is judged by.

items.concern: Hermitian (conjugate) symmetry of the random initial condition and of the stochastic forcing
items.reference_practice: Rogallo 1981, appendix: random-phase initial fields must be constructed with explicit conjugate symmetry û(−k)=û*(k) or the physical field is not real — a classic pitfall; the same applies to the Eswaran & Pope 1988 stochastic forcing's complex mode processes.
items.our_evidence: Present by construction — both noise sources are drawn in physical space and transformed, which makes the symmetry exact with no bookkeeping: src/State.jl:112–114 (`noise = new_vector_field_physical(domain); copyto!(field_data(noise), randn(…)); to_spectral!(û, noise, …)`, same for the scalar at 203–205), and src/Forcing.jl:747–748 (`randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical)); to_spectral!(…)`) with the docstring stating the intent at Forcing.jl:680–682: "generated as a real physical field, transformed, and band-limited — guaranteeing a valid real field with no Hermitian-symmetry bookkeeping".
items.consequence_if_missing: A non-Hermitian spectrum means the nominal physical field is complex; an r2c inverse silently takes the Hermitian part, giving a field whose spectrum is not the one prescribed — wrong initial statistics and forcing statistics with no error raised.

items.concern: Conjugate-symmetry (reality) drift of the evolving state over long runs
items.reference_practice: Codes that store the full complex cube re-enforce symmetry periodically or zero the oddball each step (GHOST and hit3d carry such special cases; the concern is noted in Canuto et al.'s treatment of real transforms). With half-spectrum (r2c) storage the constraint survives only inside the kx=0 and kx=Nyquist planes and must not be broken by any per-mode operation.
items.our_evidence: The state lives only in spectral representation (src/State.jl:58–61) and is advanced exclusively by (a) real radial symbols via `exponential_convolve!` (Propagator.jl:130–146), (b) linear combinations with real coefficients, and (c) RHS terms produced by `to_spectral!` of real physical-space products (Generator.jl:521–523, 675–678); the PhaseShift translation symbol e^{iκ·δ} is conjugate-symmetric. No operation can break the planes' internal symmetry beyond roundoff, and every nonlinear assembly passes through real physical space, so there is no re-symmetrization pass and none is needed.
items.consequence_if_missing: In a full-complex code, symmetry drift makes the field effectively complex and diagnostics quietly wrong; here the storage layout plus symbol discipline closes the channel structurally.

items.concern: Advective CFL ceiling derived from the scheme's imaginary-axis stability limit and the retained band
items.reference_practice: Pope 2000 §9.2 (Courant number ≲ 0.5–1 for pseudospectral DNS); the standard estimate Δt·κ_max·u_max ≤ y_s with y_s the scheme's imaginary-axis limit (√3 for the Williamson RK3 family) — Canuto et al. 2007, stability of RK time discretizations; codes scale the ceiling by the dealiasing cutoff since κ_max sets the largest advective eigenvalue.
items.our_evidence: src/Propagator.jl:598–608: `_base_cfl(::IFLowStorageRK3) = 0.5` (derived from y_s = √3, taken conservatively; docstring lines 560–585 derive it), `_base_cfl(::IFRK2) = 0.25` (documented as empirical since IFRK2 is imaginary-axis unstable), and `recommended_cfl(scheme, domain) = _base_cfl(scheme) * (2//3) / _retained_nyquist_fraction(domain.dealiasing)` — the ceiling shrinks automatically for HouLi/PhaseShift's wider bands. Adaptive Δt = C·Δx/u_max at src/SimulationRun.jl:516 from the cached max_speed; no `::AbstractIntegrator` fallback, so a new scheme must declare its limit (comment at 592–597).
items.consequence_if_missing: An advectively unstable step: energy piles at the truncation wavenumber and the run blows up, or — with a fallback constant — a new scheme is silently handed too large a step.

items.concern: Viscous/diffusive stability limit, and the timestep runaway of a decaying flow
items.reference_practice: Rogallo 1981 removes the viscous limit exactly with the integrating-factor transformation exp(νk²t) — the standard IF/ETD treatment (Canuto et al. 2007 on integrating factors); for the dt runaway as u_max→0, reference codes use ad-hoc caps: hit3d limits dt growth to 1% per step with a hard min(DT, 0.01), Fluidsim caps at deltat_max.
items.our_evidence: The diffusive part is advanced machine-exactly per mode — src/Generator.jl:539–545: E(κ) = exp((A(κ) − ν|κ|²)τ), "machine-exact, with no stability restriction" — so no viscous dt bound exists to enforce. The runaway is bounded by a constant-free resolution bound: src/SimulationRun.jl:493–519, `resolution = 1 / (diffusivity * κ_min^2)` with the comment deriving it (a step longer than 1/(D·κ_min²) e-folds the slowest mode in one step) and explicitly comparing hit3d's and fluidsim's caps; plus the caller's `max_dt` ceiling.
items.consequence_if_missing: Either a viscous instability (in an explicit-diffusion code) or, in decay, Δt → ~1e15 (measured, per the comment) where the integrating factor annihilates every mode and the clock advances meaninglessly.

items.concern: Blow-up (non-finite field) detection every iteration, for the scalar as well as the velocity
items.reference_practice: Not a textbook theorem but universal reference-code practice (hit3d and TurTLE both abort on non-finite diagnostics/courant checks): detect NaN/Inf promptly so a diverged run fails loudly instead of marching garbage.
items.our_evidence: src/SimulationRun.jl:579–587: after the closing deposit, `isfinite(max_speed(sim.cache)) || error("non-finite velocity at step …")` and — because a passive scalar cannot feed back into the guarded velocity — a separate `isfinite(scalar_variance(...)) || error("non-finite scalar …")`, with the comment naming exactly that one-way-coupling hole; the adaptive path also guards in cfl_timestep (line 486).
items.consequence_if_missing: A blown-up run keeps stepping (NaN velocities still give finite-looking control flow), wasting the whole allocation and, worse, a NaN scalar under a finite velocity reports success on a ruined field.

items.concern: Forcing-amplitude normalization when the forced band is empty or near-empty
items.reference_practice: Band forcings normalize by the band's own energy (Eswaran & Pope 1988 lineage), so the division needs a floor: TurTLE guards it with `if (energy_in_shell < 10*eps) energy_in_shell = 1` — an epsilon-relative substitute denominator.
items.our_evidence: src/Forcing.jl:641–646: `_injection_amplitude` returns amplitude 0 on an empty band, with the comment quoting TurTLE's guard verbatim; the emptiness test `_band_is_empty` (Forcing.jl:88–97) is deliberately scale-free (positivity + finiteness, no absolute floor — the comment explains a constant floor breaks the scalar's exact scaling symmetry, especially in Float32); VarianceRescaling returns the field untouched on an empty band (line 385) and its docstring documents the `:total` band-zeroing extreme; VarianceController zeroes its amplitude the same way (line 620).
items.consequence_if_missing: Division by ~0 hands the band an unbounded kick — immediate blow-up from an innocent configuration (a scalar seeded outside the forced shells, or the step after a :total rescale zeroed the band).

items.concern: Forcing bands structurally exclude the κ=0 mode
items.reference_practice: Eswaran & Pope 1988 (and all band-forcing descendants) force shells 0 < |k| ≤ K_F; reference implementations start their shell loops at 1, so the mean mode is unreachable by construction.
items.our_evidence: src/Forcing.jl:266–270: `_shell_band(domain, lowest, highest)` builds the band [(lowest−0.5)·k0, (highest+0.5)·k0], so the default `lowest_shell = 1` excludes κ=0 (lower edge 0.5·k0) — but `lowest_shell = 0` is accepted by every constructor with no guard, which puts κ=0 inside the band; and the additive-source hook runs after the mean-mode zeroing by deliberate design (Generator.jl:411–414: "a forcing that deliberately drives a mean remains expressible and honest"). For `Linear`, a shell-0 band folds a positive rate on the mean mode into the integrating factor (Forcing.jl:478–482) — exponential growth of û(0) with nothing damping it.
items.consequence_if_missing: A one-character misconfiguration (lowest_shell = 0) silently drives a uniform mean flow — for Linear, exponentially — reproducing exactly the pathology the mean-mode pinning was landed to remove, through a channel the pinning deliberately does not cover.

items.concern: Energy-spectrum shell-binning conventions at the first and last shell
items.reference_practice: The standard convention (Kaneda–Ishihara-style DNS reporting; Pope 2000 §6.5 distinguishes the continuous density E(κ) from discrete shell sums): shells of width 2π/L centered on integer multiples, shell m collecting |κ| ∈ [m−½, m+½); shell 0 holds only the mean mode; completeness — the shell sums must reproduce the total energy; the mean shell is excluded from scale integrals.
items.our_evidence: The binning is PF's (clone, inspiration/GBGPeriodicFields/src/Reductions.jl:1092–1093: "shells run 0…corner at the box-fundamental width, so ∑ over shells = the spectral inner exactly"; shell = round(|k|/fundamental) at 1076). Our layer documents the convention and its trap explicitly — src/Observables.jl:320–325: per-shell energy E_n with k = ΣE_n, "differ by the shell width Δκ = 2π/L and are not interchangeable" from a density; `integral_scale` excludes the κ=0 shell in both sums with a comment on why (Observables.jl:374–380) and throws on a zero-energy spectrum rather than returning NaN (383–387). All retained shells are complete spheres since every cutoff ≤ κ_Ny stays inside the cube for κ ≤ (2/3)κ_Ny and PhaseShift's 2√2/3·κ_Ny ball still fits the corner (√2·N/3 < √3·N/2).
items.consequence_if_missing: Mean-mode energy contaminates the low shells and the L11 integral (which weights them most); a shell/density confusion mis-scales every comparison against a model spectrum by Δκ.

items.concern: Checkpoint / bit-exact restart, including RNG state
items.reference_practice: Universal production-DNS practice since the Rogallo era: periodic restart files carrying the full spectral state, the clock, and the forcing's stochastic state so a run resumes bit-exactly (TurTLE checkpoints fields + particle state to HDF5; hit3d writes restart dumps).
items.our_evidence: Searched src/*.jl for checkpoint|serialize|save|resume|restart|JLD|HDF5: the only hits are Particles.restart! (a history discard after reseeding, Particles.jl:230–247) and the reproducibility seeds — `rng` keywords threaded through seeding (SimulationRun.jl:281, State.jl:110) and StochasticOU's `seed = 0` MersenneTwister (Forcing.jl:697–698, "so a forced run is reproducible"). Seeded reproducibility of a fresh run is present; persisting and resuming a running case (state + clock + OU state + RNG position + cache epochs) has no code path and no documentation.
items.consequence_if_missing: A crash or wall-clock limit loses the whole spin-up; a stochastically forced run cannot be continued reproducibly; long-run studies (the package's stated purpose includes accumulating Lagrangian statistics over long horizons) must re-warm from scratch. Possibly caller-side by design (the package leaves analysis/I-O to the caller), but nothing records that decision or tests that Julia-level serialization round-trips a live Simulation.

items.concern: Multistep (Adams–Bashforth) coefficients under an adaptive, non-uniform timestep
items.reference_practice: Hairer, Nørsett & Wanner, Solving ODEs I, §III.5: variable-step multistep methods must recompute their coefficients from the actual step history; classical fixed-step AB weights applied to varying steps silently lose order. (TurTLE sidesteps it by running AB4 at fixed dt.)
items.our_evidence: src/Particles.jl:303–305 (AdamsBashforth docstring): "The steps are **not** assumed uniform: the advective-CFL loop changes Δt every iteration, which classical fixed-step coefficients would silently get wrong, so the weights are recomputed each step from the actual step history." The weight quadrature's exactness bound is enforced as an order ≤ 8 cap rather than documented (Particles.jl:346–353), and a cache too shallow for the order is a construction error (Particles.jl:392–397).
items.consequence_if_missing: Silently wrong tracer trajectories at reduced order under the default adaptive-CFL loop — no symptom, since every position stays plausible.

items.concern: Initial condition: divergence-free, dealiased, mean-zero, with a realizable target spectrum
items.reference_practice: Rogallo 1981 §3: random initial fields are constructed divergence-free (via the projection tensor), band-limited to the resolved/dealiased band, with û(0)=0 and a prescribed radial spectrum; the amplitude is then normalized to the target energy.
items.our_evidence: src/State.jl: the envelope vanishes at κ=0 — "which IS the mean removal … Without the guard the Gaussian is exp(0) = 1 there and the seed carries a uniform mean flow — measured at 13.5% of the seeded energy" (121–127, both spectrum branches and the scalar twin guard); the dealias kernel is composed into the envelope (140: `convolve!(û, û, convolve(envelope, domain.dealias))`); then `helmholtz_projection!` enforces ∇·u = 0 (141); the energy rescale refuses a fully annihilated seed instead of silently returning zero (149–153).
items.consequence_if_missing: A seeded mean flow (13.5% of the energy, measured) that nothing would remove; an un-dealiased seed puts content above the cutoff that the first RHS assembly aliases; a non-solenoidal seed breaks the dissipation observable's divergence-free precondition (Observables.jl:121–126).

lanes.mean_mode: Textbook treatment of κ=0: the mode is a free Galilean parameter that the equations themselves neither damp (viscous term ν|κ|²û vanishes) nor determine (the pressure Poisson solve |k|²p̂ = ik·N̂ is singular there — Canuto, Hussaini, Quarteroni & Zang 2007, §3.3), so homogeneous-turbulence DNS is formulated in the zero-mean frame (Pope 2000 §9.1; Rogallo 1981, NASA TM-81315, whose moving-frame formulation and random ICs carry û(0)=0) and the mode is hard-zeroed or skipped every step; analytically ⟨u×ω⟩ = 0 on a periodic box (Lamb vector = divergence + gradient), but discretely only to roundoff, and the undamped residual random-walks. The scalar mean is conserved exactly by the conservative form (∇·(uφ) has no κ=0 component), so codes seed ⟨φ⟩=0 and rely on the divergence multiplier being exactly zero there. OUR code, as of a fix landed mid-audit in response to this very finding: src/Generator.jl:405–418 defines `_zero_mean_mode!(f)` (\"The κ = 0 (mean) mode of the assembled advective term is pinned to zero EXACTLY … measured 3% of u′ after 3000 Float32 steps. Every reference DNS pins this mode.\"), called in velocity_rhs! at Generator.jl:480 and scalar_rhs! at Generator.jl:633, deliberately BETWEEN the nonlinear assembly and the additive forcing source so a mean-driving forcing stays expressible. The supporting cast: the PF projection is a guarded identity at κ=0 (ifelse-substituted denominator, no NaN — clone DifferentialOperators.jl:207–208), the integrating factor is exp(0)=1 there (Generator.jl:539–545), the ICs zero the mode via the envelope (State.jl:121–127, 210–212), and every default forcing band starts at shell 1, lower edge 0.5·(2π/L) (Forcing.jl:266–270) — the residual gap being that lowest_shell = 0 is accepted unguarded and its source is added after the pinning.
